- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after recent spikes.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >82.5) with sentiment neutral or slightly positive, true outcome often corrects sharply downward — expect mean reversion within 5–10 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >83.0), model often overshoots and continues upward; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and model still forecasts high prices, apply aggressive downward adjustment — especially if recent history shows volatility or downward momentum.
- Model tends to underreact to sentiment shifts when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.5, add 5–10% to forecast; if <0.5, subtract 5–10%.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp drop (first 5–7 days), model often misses it — adjust forecast downward by 5–10% in first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model may lag — apply 1–2 day lag correction to forecast.
